units.rightText: and that ye may teach the children of Israel all the statutes which Jehovah hath spoken unto them by Moses.

units.leftText: And Moses said to Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering that remains from the food offerings to the LORD and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is most holy.
units.rightText: And Moses spake unto Aaron, and unto Eleazar and unto Ithamar, his sons that were left, Take the meal-offering that remaineth of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire, and eat it without leaven beside the altar; for it is most holy;

units.leftText: You shall eat it in a holy place, because it is your share and your sons’ share of the food offerings to the LORD; for this is what I have been commanded.
units.rightText: and ye shall eat it in a holy place, because it is thy portion, and thy sons’ portion, of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire: for so I am commanded.

units.leftText: And you and your sons and daughters may eat the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution in a ceremonially clean place, because these portions have been assigned to you and your children from the peace offerings of the sons of Israel.
units.rightText: And the wave-breast and the heave-thigh shall ye eat in a clean place, thou, and thy sons, and thy daughters with thee: for they are given as thy portion, and thy sons’ portion, out of the sacrifices of the peace-offerings of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: They are to bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering, together with the fat portions of the food offerings, to wave as a wave offering before the LORD. It will belong permanently to you and your children, as the LORD has commanded.”
units.rightText: The heave-thigh and the wave-breast shall they bring with the offerings made by fire of the fat, to wave it for a wave-offering before Jehovah: and it shall be thine, and thy sons’ with thee, as a portion for ever; as Jehovah hath commanded.

units.leftText: Later, Moses searched carefully for the goat of the sin offering, and behold, it had been burned up. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and asked,
units.rightText: And Moses diligently sought the goat of the sin-offering, and, behold, it was burnt: and he was angry with Eleazar and with Ithamar, the sons of Aaron that were left, saying,

units.leftText: “Why didn’t you eat the sin offering in the holy place? For it is most holy; it was given to you to take away the guilt of the congregation by making atonement for them before the LORD.
units.rightText: Wherefore have ye not eaten the sin-offering in the place of the sanctuary, seeing it is most holy, and he hath given it you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before Jehovah?

units.leftText: Since its blood was not brought inside the holy place, you should have eaten it in the sanctuary area, as I commanded.”
units.rightText: Behold, the blood of it was not brought into the sanctuary within: ye should certainly have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded.

units.leftText: But Aaron replied to Moses, “Behold, this very day they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD. Since these things have happened to me, if I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been acceptable in the sight of the LORD?”
units.rightText: And Aaron spake unto Moses, Behold, this day have they offered their sin-offering and their burnt-offering before Jehovah; and there have befallen me such things as these: and if I had eaten the sin-offering to-day, would it have been well-pleasing in the sight of Jehovah?

units.leftText: And when Moses heard this explanation, he was satisfied.
units.rightText: And when Moses heard that, it was well-pleasing in his sight.

units.leftText: The LORD spoke again to Moses and Aaron, telling them,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying unto them,

units.leftText: “Say to the Israelites, ‘Of all the beasts of the earth, these ones you may eat:
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, These are the living things which ye may eat among all the beasts that are on the earth.

units.leftText: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof completely divided and that chews the cud.
units.rightText: Whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud, among the beasts, that may ye eat.

units.leftText: But of those that only chew the cud or only have a divided hoof, you are not to eat the following: The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
units.rightText: Nevertheless these shall ye not eat of them that chew the cud, or of them that part the hoof: the camel, because he cheweth the cud but parteth not the hoof, he is unclean unto you.
leftNotes: 11:4 The precise identification of some of the birds and animals in this chapter is uncertain.

units.leftText: The rock badger, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
units.rightText: And the coney, because he cheweth the cud but parteth not the hoof, he is unclean unto you.
leftNotes: 11:5 Or The coney or The hyrax

units.leftText: The rabbit, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
units.rightText: And the hare, because she cheweth the cud but parteth not the hoof, she is unclean unto you.

units.leftText: And the pig, though it has a split hoof completely divided, does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
units.rightText: And the swine, because he parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, but cheweth not the cud, he is unclean unto you.

units.leftText: You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
units.rightText: Of their flesh ye shall not eat, and their carcasses ye shall not touch; they are unclean unto you.

units.leftText: Of all the creatures that live in the water, whether in the seas or in the streams, you may eat anything with fins and scales.
units.rightText: These may ye eat of all that are in the waters: whatsoever hath fins and scales in the waters, in the seas, and in the rivers, that may ye eat.

units.leftText: But the following among all the teeming life and creatures in the water are detestable to you: everything in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales.
units.rightText: And all that have not fins and scales in the seas, and in the rivers, of all that move in the waters, and of all the living creatures that are in the waters, they are an abomination unto you,

units.leftText: They shall be an abomination to you; you must not eat their meat, and you must detest their carcasses.
units.rightText: and they shall be an abomination unto you; ye shall not eat of their flesh, and their carcasses ye shall have in abomination.

units.leftText: Everything in the water that does not have fins and scales shall be detestable to you.
units.rightText: Whatsoever hath no fins nor scales in the waters, that is an abomination unto you.

units.leftText: Additionally, you are to detest the following birds, and they must not be eaten because they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
units.rightText: And these ye shall have in abomination among the birds; they shall not be eaten, they are an abomination: the eagle, and the gier-eagle, and the ospray,

units.leftText: the kite, any kind of falcon,
units.rightText: and the kite, and the falcon after its kind,

units.leftText: any kind of raven,
units.rightText: every raven after its kind,

units.leftText: the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
units.rightText: and the ostrich, and the night-hawk, and the sea-mew, and the hawk after its kind,
leftNotes: 11:16 Literally the daughter of the ostrich or the daughter of the owl

units.leftText: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
units.rightText: and the little owl, and the cormorant, and the great owl,

units.leftText: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
units.rightText: and the horned owl, and the pelican, and the vulture,

units.leftText: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
units.rightText: and the stork, the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.

units.leftText: All flying insects that walk on all fours are detestable to you.
units.rightText: All winged creeping things that go upon all fours are an abomination unto you.

units.leftText: However, you may eat the following kinds of flying insects that walk on all fours: those having jointed legs above their feet for hopping on the ground.
units.rightText: Yet these may ye eat of all winged creeping things that go upon all fours, which have legs above their feet, wherewith to leap upon the earth;

units.leftText: Of these you may eat any kind of locust, katydid, cricket, or grasshopper.
units.rightText: even these of them ye may eat: the locust after its kind, and the bald locust after its kind, and the cricket after its kind, and the grasshopper after its kind.

units.leftText: All other flying insects that have four legs are detestable to you.
units.rightText: But all winged creeping things, which have four feet, are an abomination unto you.

units.leftText: These creatures will make you unclean. Whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
units.rightText: And by these ye shall become unclean: whosoever toucheth the carcass of them shall be unclean until the even;

units.leftText: and whoever picks up one of their carcasses must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: and whosoever beareth aught of the carcass of them shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Every animal with hooves not completely divided or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you. Whoever touches any of them will be unclean.
units.rightText: Every beast which parteth the hoof, and is not clovenfooted, nor cheweth the cud, is unclean unto you: every one that toucheth them shall be unclean.
leftNotes: 11:26 Literally a split hoof not completely divided

units.leftText: All the four-footed animals that walk on their paws are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
units.rightText: And whatsoever goeth upon its paws, among all beasts that go on all fours, they are unclean unto you: whoso toucheth their carcass shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: and anyone who picks up a carcass must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
units.rightText: And he that beareth the carcass of them shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the even: they are unclean unto you.

units.leftText: The following creatures that move along the ground are unclean for you: the mole, the mouse, any kind of great lizard,
units.rightText: And these are they which are unclean unto you among the creeping things that creep upon the earth: the weasel, and the mouse, and the great lizard after its kind,

units.leftText: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the common lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
units.rightText: and the gecko, and the land-crocodile, and the lizard, and the sand-lizard, and the chameleon.

units.leftText: These animals are unclean for you among all the crawling creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: These are they which are unclean to you among all that creep: whosoever doth touch them, when they are dead, shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: When one of them dies and falls on something, that article becomes unclean; any article of wood, clothing, leather, sackcloth, or any implement used for work must be rinsed with water and will remain unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
units.rightText: And upon whatsoever any of them, when they are dead, doth fall, it shall be unclean; whether it be any vessel of wood, or raiment, or skin, or sack, whatsoever vessel it be, wherewith any work is done, it must be put into water, and it shall be unclean until the even; then shall it be clean.

units.leftText: If any of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean; you must break the pot.
units.rightText: And every earthen vessel, whereinto any of them falleth, whatsoever is in it shall be unclean, and it ye shall break.

units.leftText: Any food coming into contact with water from that pot will be unclean, and any drink in such a container will be unclean.
units.rightText: All food therein which may be eaten, that on which water cometh, shall be unclean; and all drink that may be drunk in every such vessel shall be unclean.

units.leftText: Anything upon which one of their carcasses falls will be unclean. If it is an oven or cooking pot, it must be smashed; it is unclean and will remain unclean for you.
units.rightText: And every thing whereupon any part of their carcass falleth shall be unclean; whether oven, or range for pots, it shall be broken in pieces: they are unclean, and shall be unclean unto you.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, a spring or cistern containing water will remain clean, but one who touches a carcass in it will be unclean.
units.rightText: Nevertheless a fountain or a pit wherein is a gathering of water shall be clean: but that which toucheth their carcass shall be unclean.

units.leftText: If a carcass falls on any seed for sowing, the seed is clean;
units.rightText: And if aught of their carcass fall upon any sowing seed which is to be sown, it is clean.

units.leftText: but if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
units.rightText: But if water be put upon the seed, and aught of their carcass fall thereon, it is unclean unto you.

units.leftText: If an animal that you may eat dies, anyone who touches the carcass will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And if any beast, of which ye may eat, die; he that toucheth the carcass thereof shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Whoever eats from the carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening, and anyone who picks up the carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And he that eateth of the carcass of it shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the even: he also that beareth the carcass of it shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Every creature that moves along the ground is detestable; it must not be eaten.
units.rightText: And every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth is an abomination; it shall not be eaten.

units.leftText: Do not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it crawls on its belly or walks on four or more feet; for such creatures are detestable.
units.rightText: Whatsoever goeth upon the belly, and whatsoever goeth upon all fours, or whatsoever hath many feet, even all creeping things that creep upon the earth, them ye shall not eat; for they are an abomination.

units.leftText: Do not defile yourselves by any crawling creature; do not become unclean or defiled by them.
units.rightText: Ye shall not make yourselves abominable with any creeping thing that creepeth, neither shall ye make yourselves unclean with them, that ye should be defiled thereby.

units.leftText: For I am the LORD your God; consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am holy. You must not defile yourselves by any creature that crawls along the ground.
units.rightText: For I am Jehovah your God: sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that moveth upon the earth.
leftNotes: 11:44 Here and in verse 45; cited in 1 Peter 1:16|1PE 1:16*

units.leftText: For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt so that I would be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy.
units.rightText: For I am Jehovah that brought you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.

units.leftText: This is the law regarding animals, birds, all living creatures that move in the water, and all creatures that crawl along the ground.
units.rightText: This is the law of the beast, and of the bird, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth;

units.leftText: You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between animals that may be eaten and those that may not.’”
units.rightText: to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the living thing that may be eaten and the living thing that may not be eaten.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Say to the Israelites, ‘A woman who becomes pregnant and gives birth to a son will be unclean for seven days, as she is during the days of her menstruation.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a woman conceive seed, and bear a man-child, then she shall be unclean seven days; as in the days of the impurity of her sickness shall she be unclean.

units.leftText: And on the eighth day the flesh of the boy’s foreskin is to be circumcised.
units.rightText: And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

units.leftText: The woman shall continue in purification from her bleeding for thirty-three days. She must not touch anything sacred or go into the sanctuary until the days of her purification are complete.
units.rightText: And she shall continue in the blood of her purifying three and thirty days; she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.

units.leftText: If, however, she gives birth to a daughter, the woman will be unclean for two weeks as she is during her menstruation. Then she must continue in purification from her bleeding for sixty-six days.
units.rightText: But if she bear a maid-child, then she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her impurity; and she shall continue in the blood of her purifying threescore and six days.

units.leftText: When the days of her purification are complete, whether for a son or for a daughter, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.
units.rightText: And when the days of her purifying are fulfilled, for a son, or for a daughter, she shall bring a lamb a year old for a burnt-offering, and a young pigeon, or a turtle-dove, for a sin-offering, unto the door of the tent of meeting, unto the priest:

units.leftText: And the priest will present them before the LORD and make atonement for her; and she shall be ceremonially cleansed from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman giving birth, whether to a male or to a female.
units.rightText: and he shall offer it before Jehovah, and make atonement for her; and she shall be cleansed from the fountain of her blood. This is the law for her that beareth, whether a male or a female.

units.leftText: But if she cannot afford a lamb, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. Then the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.’”
units.rightText: And if her means suffice not for a lamb, then she shall take two turtle-doves, or two young pigeons; the one for a burnt-offering, and the other for a sin-offering: and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.
leftNotes: 12:8 Cited in Luke 2:24|LUK 2:24*

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

units.leftText: “When someone has a swelling or rash or bright spot on his skin that may be an infectious skin disease, he must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest.
units.rightText: When a man shall have in the skin of his flesh a rising, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it become in the skin of his flesh the plague of leprosy, then he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest, or unto one of his sons the priests:
leftNotes: 13:2 Forms of the Hebrew tzaraath, traditionally translated as leprosy, were used for various skin diseases; here and throughout verses 3–46.

units.leftText: The priest is to examine the infection on his skin, and if the hair in the infection has turned white and the sore appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look on the plague in the skin of the flesh: and if the hair in the plague be turned white, and the appearance of the plague be deeper than the skin of his flesh, it is the plague of leprosy; and the priest shall look on him, and pronounce him unclean.

units.leftText: If, however, the spot on his skin is white and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
units.rightText: And if the bright spot be white in the skin of his flesh, and the appearance thereof be not deeper than the skin, and the hair thereof be not turned white, then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague seven days:

units.leftText: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if he sees that the infection is unchanged and has not spread on the skin, the priest must isolate him for another seven days.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look on him the seventh day: and, behold, if in his eyes the plague be at a stay, and the plague be not spread in the skin, then the priest shall shut him up seven days more:

units.leftText: The priest will examine him again on the seventh day, and if the sore has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash. The person must wash his clothes and be clean.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look on him again the seventh day; and, behold, if the plague be dim, and the plague be not spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean: it is a scab: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean.

units.leftText: But if the rash spreads further on his skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he must present himself again to the priest.
units.rightText: But if the scab spread abroad in the skin, after that he hath showed himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall show himself to the priest again:

units.leftText: The priest will reexamine him, and if the rash has spread on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a skin disease.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look; and, behold, if the scab be spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is leprosy.

units.leftText: When anyone develops a skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.
units.rightText: When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought unto the priest;

units.leftText: The priest will examine him, and if there is a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
units.rightText: and the priest shall look; and, behold, if there be a white rising in the skin, and it have turned the hair white, and there be quick raw flesh in the rising,

units.leftText: it is a chronic skin disease and the priest must pronounce him unclean. He need not isolate him, for he is unclean.
units.rightText: it is an old leprosy in the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean: he shall not shut him up; for he is unclean.

units.leftText: But if the skin disease breaks out all over his skin so that it covers all the skin of the infected person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
units.rightText: And if the leprosy break out abroad in the skin, and the leprosy cover all the skin of him that hath the plague from his head even to his feet, as far as appeareth to the priest;

units.leftText: the priest shall examine him, and if the disease has covered his entire body, he is to pronounce the infected person clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.
units.rightText: then the priest shall look; and, behold, if the leprosy have covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him clean that hath the plague: it is all turned white: he is clean.

units.leftText: But whenever raw flesh appears on someone, he will be unclean.
units.rightText: But whensoever raw flesh appeareth in him, he shall be unclean.

units.leftText: When the priest sees the raw flesh, he must pronounce him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; it is a skin disease.
units.rightText: And the priest shall look on the raw flesh, and pronounce him unclean: the raw flesh is unclean: it is leprosy.

units.leftText: But if the raw flesh changes and turns white, he must go to the priest.
units.rightText: Or if the raw flesh turn again, and be changed unto white, then he shall come unto the priest;

units.leftText: The priest will reexamine him, and if the infection has turned white, the priest is to pronounce the infected person clean; then he is clean.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look on him; and, behold, if the plague be turned into white, then the priest shall pronounce him clean that hath the plague: he is clean.

units.leftText: When a boil appears on someone’s skin and it heals,
units.rightText: And when the flesh hath in the skin thereof a boil, and it is healed,

units.leftText: and a white swelling or a reddish-white spot develops where the boil was, he must present himself to the priest.
units.rightText: and in the place of the boil there is a white rising, or a bright spot, reddish-white, then it shall be showed to the priest;

units.leftText: The priest shall examine it, and if it appears to be beneath the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection that has broken out in the boil.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look; and, behold, if the appearance thereof be lower than the skin, and the hair thereof be turned white, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy, it hath broken out in the boil.

units.leftText: But when the priest examines it, if there is no white hair in it, and it is not beneath the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
units.rightText: But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no white hairs therein, and it be not lower than the skin, but be dim; then the priest shall shut him up seven days:

units.leftText: If it spreads any further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is an infection.
units.rightText: and if it spread abroad in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a plague.

units.leftText: But if the spot remains unchanged and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
units.rightText: But if the bright spot stay in its place, and be not spread, it is the scar of the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.

units.leftText: When there is a burn on someone’s skin and the raw area of the burn becomes reddish-white or white,
units.rightText: Or when the flesh hath in the skin thereof a burning by fire, and the quick flesh of the burning become a bright spot, reddish-white, or white;

units.leftText: the priest must examine it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
units.rightText: then the priest shall look upon it; and, behold, if the hair in the bright spot be turned white, and the appearance thereof be deeper than the skin; it is leprosy, it hath broken out in the burning: and the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy.

units.leftText: But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not beneath the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
units.rightText: But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no white hair in the bright spot, and it be no lower than the skin, but be dim; then the priest shall shut him up seven days:

units.leftText: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if it has spread further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look upon him the seventh day: if it spread abroad in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy.

units.leftText: But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread on the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest is to pronounce him clean; for it is only the scar from the burn.
units.rightText: And if the bright spot stay in its place, and be not spread in the skin, but be dim; it is the rising of the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him clean: for it is the scar of the burning.

units.leftText: If a man or woman has an infection on the head or chin,
units.rightText: And when a man or woman hath a plague upon the head or upon the beard,

units.leftText: the priest shall examine the infection, and if it appears to be deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a scaly outbreak, an infectious disease of the head or chin.
units.rightText: then the priest shall look on the plague; and, behold, if the appearance thereof be deeper than the skin, and there be in it yellow thin hair, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a scall, it is leprosy of the head or of the beard.

units.leftText: But if the priest examines the scaly infection and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
units.rightText: And if the priest look on the plague of the scall, and, behold, the appearance thereof be not deeper than the skin, and there be no black hair in it, then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague of the scall seven days:

units.leftText: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine the infection, and if the scaly outbreak has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin,
units.rightText: and in the seventh day the priest shall look on the plague; and, behold, if the scall be not spread, and there be in it no yellow hair, and the appearance of the scall be not deeper than the skin,

units.leftText: then the person must shave himself except for the scaly area. Then the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
units.rightText: then he shall be shaven, but the scall shall he not shave; and the priest shall shut up him that hath the scall seven days more:

units.leftText: On the seventh day the priest shall examine the scaly outbreak, and if it has not spread on the skin and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest is to pronounce him clean. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
units.rightText: and in the seventh day the priest shall look on the scall; and, behold, if the scall be not spread in the skin, and the appearance thereof be not deeper than the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him clean: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean.

units.leftText: If, however, the scaly outbreak spreads further on the skin after his cleansing,
units.rightText: But if the scall spread abroad in the skin after his cleansing,

units.leftText: the priest is to examine him, and if the scaly outbreak has spread on the skin, the priest need not look for yellow hair; the person is unclean.
units.rightText: then the priest shall look on him; and, behold, if the scall be spread in the skin, the priest shall not seek for the yellow hair; he is unclean.

units.leftText: If, however, in his sight the scaly outbreak is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, then it has healed. He is clean, and the priest is to pronounce him clean.
units.rightText: But if in his eyes the scall be at a stay, and black hair be grown up therein; the scall is healed, he is clean: and the priest shall pronounce him clean.

units.leftText: When a man or a woman has white spots on the skin,
units.rightText: And when a man or a woman hath in the skin of the flesh bright spots, even white bright spots;

units.leftText: the priest shall examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.
units.rightText: then the priest shall look; and, behold, if the bright spots in the skin of their flesh be of a dull white, it is a tetter, it hath broken out in the skin; he is clean.

units.leftText: Now if a man loses his hair and is bald, he is still clean.
units.rightText: And if a man’s hair be fallen off his head, he is bald; yet is he clean.

units.leftText: Or if his hairline recedes and he is bald on his forehead, he is still clean.
units.rightText: And if his hair be fallen off from the front part of his head, he is forehead bald; yet is he clean.

units.leftText: But if there is a reddish-white sore on the bald head or forehead, it is an infectious disease breaking out on it.
units.rightText: But if there be in the bald head, or the bald forehead, a reddish-white plague; it is leprosy breaking out in his bald head, or his bald forehead.

units.leftText: The priest is to examine him, and if the swelling of the infection on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white like a skin disease,
units.rightText: Then the priest shall look upon him; and, behold, if the rising of the plague be reddish-white in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, as the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the flesh;

units.leftText: the man is diseased; he is unclean. The priest must pronounce him unclean because of the infection on his head.
units.rightText: he is a leprous man, he is unclean: the priest shall surely pronounce him unclean; his plague is in his head.

units.leftText: A diseased person must wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose, and he must cover his mouth and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean!’
units.rightText: And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and the hair of his head shall go loose, and he shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean.
leftNotes: 13:45 Or uncover his head

units.leftText: As long as he has the infection, he remains unclean. He must live alone in a place outside the camp. Laws about Mildew
units.rightText: All the days wherein the plague is in him he shall be unclean; he is unclean: he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his dwelling be.

units.leftText: If any fabric is contaminated with mildew — any wool or linen garment,
units.rightText: The garment also that the plague of leprosy is in, whether it be a woollen garment, or a linen garment;
leftNotes: 13:47 Forms of the Hebrew tzaraath, traditionally translated as leprosy regarding skin diseases, are translated as mildew regarding blemishes on garments, utensils, or buildings; here and throughout the remainder of this chapter.

units.leftText: any weave or knit of linen or wool, or any article of leather—
units.rightText: whether it be in warp, or woof; of linen, or of woollen; whether in a skin, or in anything made of skin;

units.leftText: and if the mark in the fabric, leather, weave, knit, or leather article is green or red, then it is contaminated with mildew and must be shown to the priest.
units.rightText: if the plague be greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the skin, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything of skin; it is the plague of leprosy, and shall be showed unto the priest.

units.leftText: And the priest is to examine the mildew and isolate the contaminated fabric for seven days.
units.rightText: And the priest shall look upon the plague, and shut up that which hath the plague seven days:

units.leftText: On the seventh day the priest shall reexamine it, and if the mildew has spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather, then regardless of how it is used, it is a harmful mildew; the article is unclean.
units.rightText: and he shall look on the plague on the seventh day: if the plague be spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in the skin, whatever service skin is used for; the plague is a fretting leprosy; it is unclean.

units.leftText: He is to burn the fabric, weave, or knit, whether the contaminated item is wool or linen or leather. Since the mildew is harmful, the article must be burned up.
units.rightText: And he shall burn the garment, whether the warp or the woof, in woollen or in linen, or anything of skin, wherein the plague is: for it is a fretting leprosy; it shall be burnt in the fire.

units.leftText: But when the priest reexamines it, if the mildew has not spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather article,
units.rightText: And if the priest shall look, and, behold, the plague be not spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything of skin;

units.leftText: the priest is to order the contaminated article to be washed and isolated for another seven days.
units.rightText: then the priest shall command that they wash the thing wherein the plague is, and he shall shut it up seven days more:

units.leftText: After it has been washed, the priest is to reexamine it, and if the mildewed article has not changed in appearance, it is unclean. Even though the mildew has not spread, you must burn it, whether the rot is on the front or back.
units.rightText: and the priest shall look, after that the plague is washed; and, behold, if the plague have not changed its color, and the plague be not spread, it is unclean; thou shalt burn it in the fire: it is a fret, whether the bareness be within or without.

units.leftText: If the priest examines it and the mildew has faded after it has been washed, he must cut the contaminated section out of the fabric, leather, weave, or knit.
units.rightText: And if the priest look, and, behold, the plague be dim after the washing thereof, then he shall rend it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the woof:

units.leftText: But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.
units.rightText: and if it appear still in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in anything of skin, it is breaking out: thou shalt burn that wherein the plague is with fire.

units.leftText: If the mildew disappears from the fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article after washing, then it is to be washed again, and it will be clean.
units.rightText: And the garment, either the warp, or the woof, or whatsoever thing of skin it be, which thou shalt wash, if the plague be departed from them, then it shall be washed the second time, and shall be clean.

units.leftText: This is the law concerning a mildew contamination in wool or linen fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article, for pronouncing it clean or unclean.”
units.rightText: This is the law of the plague of leprosy in a garment of woollen or linen, either in the warp, or the woof, or anything of skin, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “This is the law for the one afflicted with a skin disease on the day of his cleansing, when he is brought to the priest.
units.rightText: This shall be the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing: he shall be brought unto the priest:
leftNotes: 14:2 Forms of the Hebrew tzaraath, traditionally translated as leprosy, were used for various skin diseases; also in verses 3, 7, 32, 54, and 57.

units.leftText: The priest is to go outside the camp to examine him, and if the skin disease of the afflicted person has healed,
units.rightText: and the priest shall go forth out of the camp; and the priest shall look; and, behold, if the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper,

units.leftText: the priest shall order that two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be brought for the one to be cleansed.
units.rightText: then shall the priest command to take for him that is to be cleansed two living clean birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop:

units.leftText: Then the priest shall command that one of the birds be slaughtered over fresh water in a clay pot.
units.rightText: and the priest shall command to kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water.
leftNotes: 14:5 Or flowing water or living water; here and in verses 6, 50, 51, and 52

units.leftText: And he is to take the live bird together with the cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop, and dip them into the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the fresh water.
units.rightText: As for the living bird, he shall take it, and the cedar wood, and the scarlet, and the hyssop, and shall dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that was killed over the running water:

units.leftText: Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the skin disease. Then he shall pronounce him clean and release the live bird into the open field.
units.rightText: and he shall sprinkle upon him that is to be cleansed from the leprosy seven times, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let go the living bird into the open field.

units.leftText: The one being cleansed must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe with water; then he will be ceremonially clean. Afterward, he may enter the camp, but he must remain outside his tent for seven days.
units.rightText: And he that is to be cleansed shall wash his clothes, and shave off all his hair, and bathe himself in water; and he shall be clean: and after that he shall come into the camp, but shall dwell outside his tent seven days.

units.leftText: On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair — his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and the rest of his hair. He must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and he will be clean.
units.rightText: And it shall be on the seventh day, that he shall shave all his hair off his head and his beard and his eyebrows, even all his hair he shall shave off: and he shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and he shall be clean.

units.leftText: On the eighth day he is to bring two unblemished male lambs, an unblemished ewe lamb a year old, a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with olive oil, and one log of olive oil.
units.rightText: And on the eighth day he shall take two he-lambs without blemish, and one ewe-lamb a year old without blemish, and three tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, and one log of oil.
leftNotes: 14:10 Three-tenths of an ephah is approximately 6 dry quarts or 6.6 liters (probably about 7.6 pounds or 3.5 kilograms of flour).
14:10 Or one log of oil; that is, approximately 0.33 quarts or 0.31 liters; also in verses 12, 15, 21, and 24

units.leftText: The priest who performs the cleansing shall present the one to be cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And the priest that cleanseth him shall set the man that is to be cleansed, and those things, before Jehovah, at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: Then the priest is to take one of the male lambs and present it as a guilt offering, along with the log of olive oil; and he must wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
units.rightText: And the priest shall take one of the he-lambs, and offer him for a trespass-offering, and the log of oil, and wave them for a wave-offering before Jehovah:

units.leftText: Then he is to slaughter the lamb in the sanctuary area where the sin offering and burnt offering are slaughtered. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest; it is most holy.
units.rightText: and he shall kill the he-lamb in the place where they kill the sin-offering and the burnt-offering, in the place of the sanctuary: for as the sin-offering is the priest’s, so is the trespass-offering: it is most holy.

units.leftText: The priest is to take some of the blood from the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
units.rightText: And the priest shall take of the blood of the trespass-offering, and the priest shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.

units.leftText: Then the priest shall take some of the log of olive oil, pour it into his left palm,
units.rightText: And the priest shall take of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his own left hand;

units.leftText: dip his right forefinger into the oil in his left palm, and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.
units.rightText: and the priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle of the oil with his finger seven times before Jehovah.

units.leftText: And the priest is to put some of the oil remaining in his palm on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
units.rightText: And of the rest of the oil that is in his hand shall the priest put upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, upon the blood of the trespass-offering:

units.leftText: The rest of the oil in his palm, the priest is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
units.rightText: and the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put upon the head of him that is to be cleansed: and the priest shall make atonement for him before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then the priest is to sacrifice the sin offering and make atonement for the one to be cleansed from his uncleanness. After that, the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering
units.rightText: And the priest shall offer the sin-offering, and make atonement for him that is to be cleansed because of his uncleanness: and afterward he shall kill the burnt-offering;

units.leftText: and offer it on the altar, with the grain offering, to make atonement for him, and he will be clean.
units.rightText: and the priest shall offer the burnt-offering and the meal-offering upon the altar: and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

units.leftText: If, however, the person is poor and cannot afford these offerings, he is to take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved to make atonement for him, along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, a log of olive oil,
units.rightText: And if he be poor, and cannot get so much, then he shall take one he-lamb for a trespass-offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one tenth part of an ephah of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering, and a log of oil;
leftNotes: 14:21 A tenth of an ephah is approximately 2 dry quarts or 2.2 liters (probably about 2.6 pounds or 1.2 kilograms of flour).

units.leftText: and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford, one to be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
units.rightText: and two turtle-doves, or two young pigeons, such as he is able to get; and the one shall be a sin-offering, and the other a burnt-offering.

units.leftText: On the eighth day he is to bring them for his cleansing to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD.
units.rightText: And on the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing unto the priest, unto the door of the tent of meeting, before Jehovah:

units.leftText: The priest shall take the lamb for the guilt offering, along with the log of olive oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
units.rightText: and the priest shall take the lamb of the trespass-offering, and the log of oil, and the priest shall wave them for a wave-offering before Jehovah.

units.leftText: And after he slaughters the lamb for the guilt offering, the priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
units.rightText: And he shall kill the lamb of the trespass-offering; and the priest shall take of the blood of the trespass-offering, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.

units.leftText: Then the priest is to pour some of the oil into his left palm
units.rightText: And the priest shall pour of the oil into the palm of his own left hand;

units.leftText: and sprinkle with his right forefinger some of the oil in his left palm seven times before the LORD.
units.rightText: and the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before Jehovah:

units.leftText: The priest shall also put some of the oil in his palm on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot — on the same places as the blood of the guilt offering.
units.rightText: and the priest shall put of the oil that is in his hand upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the trespass-offering:

units.leftText: The rest of the oil in his palm, the priest is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
units.rightText: and the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then he must sacrifice the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford,
units.rightText: And he shall offer one of the turtle-doves, or of the young pigeons, such as he is able to get,

units.leftText: one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make atonement before the LORD for the one to be cleansed.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

units.leftText: “When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I put a contamination of mildew into a house in that land,
units.rightText: When ye are come into the land of Canaan, which I give to you for a possession, and I put the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of your possession;
leftNotes: 14:34 Forms of the Hebrew tzaraath, traditionally translated as leprosy regarding skin diseases, are translated as mildew regarding blemishes on garments, utensils, or buildings; here and throughout the remainder of this chapter.

units.leftText: the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, ‘Something like mildew has appeared in my house.’
units.rightText: then he that owneth the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, There seemeth to me to be as it were a plague in the house.

units.leftText: The priest must order that the house be cleared before he enters it to examine the mildew, so that nothing in the house will become unclean. After this, the priest shall go in to inspect the house.
units.rightText: And the priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest goeth in to see the plague, that all that is in the house be not made unclean: and afterward the priest shall go in to see the house:

units.leftText: He is to examine the house, and if the mildew on the walls consists of green or red depressions that appear to be beneath the surface of the wall,
units.rightText: and he shall look on the plague; and, behold, if the plague be in the walls of the house with hollow streaks, greenish or reddish, and the appearance thereof be lower than the wall;

units.leftText: the priest shall go outside the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days.
units.rightText: then the priest shall go out of the house to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days.

units.leftText: On the seventh day the priest is to return and inspect the house. If the mildew has spread on the walls,
units.rightText: And the priest shall come again the seventh day, and shall look; and, behold, if the plague be spread in the walls of the house;

units.leftText: he must order that the contaminated stones be pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the city.
units.rightText: then the priest shall command that they take out the stones in which the plague is, and cast them into an unclean place without the city:

units.leftText: And he shall have the inside of the house scraped completely and the plaster that is scraped off dumped into an unclean place outside the city.
units.rightText: and he shall cause the house to be scraped within round about, and they shall pour out the mortar, that they scrape off, without the city into an unclean place:

units.leftText: So different stones must be obtained to replace the contaminated ones, as well as additional mortar to replaster the house.
units.rightText: and they shall take other stones, and put them in the place of those stones; and he shall take other mortar, and shall plaster the house.

units.leftText: If the mildew reappears in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house has been scraped and replastered,
units.rightText: And if the plague come again, and break out in the house, after that he hath taken out the stones, and after he hath scraped the house, and after it is plastered;

units.leftText: the priest must come and inspect it.
units.rightText: then the priest shall come in and look; and, behold, if the plague be spread in the house, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean.

units.leftText: It must be torn down with its stones, its timbers, and all its plaster, and taken outside the city to an unclean place.
units.rightText: And he shall break down the house, the stones of it, and the timber thereof, and all the mortar of the house; and he shall carry them forth out of the city into an unclean place.

units.leftText: Anyone who enters the house during any of the days that it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: Moreover he that goeth into the house all the while that it is shut up shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: And anyone who sleeps in the house or eats in it must wash his clothes. Cleansing a Home
units.rightText: And he that lieth in the house shall wash his clothes; and he that eateth in the house shall wash his clothes.

units.leftText: If, however, the priest comes and inspects it, and the mildew has not spread after the house has been replastered, he shall pronounce the house clean, because the mildew is gone.
units.rightText: And if the priest shall come in, and look, and, behold, the plague hath not spread in the house, after the house was plastered; then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.

units.leftText: He is to take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop to purify the house;
units.rightText: And he shall take to cleanse the house two birds, and cedar-wood, and scarlet, and hyssop:

units.leftText: and he shall slaughter one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.
units.rightText: and he shall kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water:

units.leftText: Then he shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn, and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
units.rightText: and he shall take the cedar-wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slain bird, and in the running water, and sprinkle the house seven times:

units.leftText: And he shall cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.
units.rightText: and he shall cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, and with the running water, and with the living bird, and with the cedar-wood, and with the hyssop, and with the scarlet:

units.leftText: Finally, he is to release the live bird into the open fields outside the city. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.
units.rightText: but he shall let go the living bird out of the city into the open field: so shall he make atonement for the house; and it shall be clean.

units.leftText: This is the law for any infectious skin disease, for a scaly outbreak,
units.rightText: This is the law for all manner of plague of leprosy, and for a scall,

units.leftText: for mildew in clothing or in a house,
units.rightText: and for the leprosy of a garment, and for a house,

units.leftText: and for a swelling, rash, or spot,
units.rightText: and for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot;

units.leftText: to determine when something is clean or unclean. This is the law regarding skin diseases and mildew. ”
units.rightText: to teach when it is unclean, and when it is clean: this is the law of leprosy.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying,

units.leftText: “Say to the Israelites, ‘When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean.
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When any man hath an issue out of his flesh, because of his issue he is unclean.

units.leftText: This uncleanness is from his discharge, whether his body allows the discharge to flow or blocks it. So his discharge will bring about uncleanness.
units.rightText: And this shall be his uncleanness in his issue: whether his flesh run with his issue, or his flesh be stopped from his issue, it is his uncleanness.

units.leftText: Any bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and any furniture on which he sits will be unclean.
units.rightText: Every bed whereon he that hath the issue lieth shall be unclean; and everything whereon he sitteth shall be unclean.

units.leftText: Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And whosoever toucheth his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Whoever sits on furniture on which the man with the discharge was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And he that sitteth on anything whereon he that hath the issue sat shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: If the man with the discharge spits on one who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And if he that hath the issue spit upon him that is clean, then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.
units.rightText: And what saddle soever he that hath the issue rideth upon shall be unclean.

units.leftText: Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And whosoever toucheth anything that was under him shall be unclean until the even: and he that beareth those things shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands with water, the one who was touched must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And whomsoever he that hath the issue toucheth, without having rinsed his hands in water, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Any clay pot that the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden utensil must be rinsed with water. The Cleansing of Men
units.rightText: And the earthen vessel, which he that hath the issue toucheth, shall be broken; and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water.

units.leftText: When the man has been cleansed from his discharge, he must count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe himself in fresh water, and he shall be clean.
units.rightText: And when he that hath an issue is cleansed of his issue, then he shall number to himself seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in running water, and shall be clean.
leftNotes: 15:13 Or flowing water or living water

units.leftText: On the eighth day he is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
units.rightText: And on the eighth day he shall take to him two turtle-doves, or two young pigeons, and come before Jehovah unto the door of the tent of meeting, and give them unto the priest:

units.leftText: The priest is to sacrifice them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge.
units.rightText: and the priest shall offer them, the one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him before Jehovah for his issue.

units.leftText: When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And if any man’s seed of copulation go out from him, then he shall bathe all his flesh in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Any clothing or leather on which there is an emission of semen must be washed with water, and it will remain unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And every garment, and every skin, whereon is the seed of copulation, shall be washed with water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both must bathe with water, and they will remain unclean until evening. The Uncleanness of Women
units.rightText: The woman also with whom a man shall lie with seed of copulation, they shall both bathe themselves in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: When a woman has a discharge consisting of blood from her body, she will be unclean due to her menstruation for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be in her impurity seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Anything on which she lies or sits during her menstruation will be unclean,
units.rightText: And everything that she lieth upon in her impurity shall be unclean: everything also that she sitteth upon shall be unclean.

units.leftText: and anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And whosoever toucheth her bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: Whoever touches any furniture on which she was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And whosoever toucheth anything that she sitteth upon shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: And whether it is a bed or furniture on which she was sitting, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
units.rightText: And if it be on the bed, or on anything whereon she sitteth, when he toucheth it, he shall be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed on which he lies will become unclean.
units.rightText: And if any man lie with her, and her impurity be upon him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed whereon he lieth shall be unclean.

units.leftText: When a woman has a discharge of her blood for many days at a time other than her menstrual period, or if it continues beyond her period, she will be unclean all the days of her unclean discharge, just as she is during the days of her menstruation.
units.rightText: And if a woman have an issue of her blood many days not in the time of her impurity, or if she have an issue beyond the time of her impurity; all the days of the issue of her uncleanness she shall be as in the days of her impurity: she is unclean.

units.leftText: Any bed on which she lies or any furniture on which she sits during the days of her discharge will be unclean, like her bed during her menstrual period.
units.rightText: Every bed whereon she lieth all the days of her issue shall be unto her as the bed of her impurity: and everything whereon she sitteth shall be unclean, as the uncleanness of her impurity.

units.leftText: Anyone who touches these things will be unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. The Cleansing of Women
units.rightText: And whosoever toucheth those things shall be unclean, and shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and be unclean until the even.

units.leftText: When a woman is cleansed of her discharge, she must count off seven days, and after that she will be ceremonially clean.
units.rightText: But if she be cleansed of her issue, then she shall number to herself seven days, and after that she shall be clean.

units.leftText: On the eighth day she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And on the eighth day she shall take unto her two turtle-doves, or two young pigeons, and bring them unto the priest, to the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: The priest is to sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge.
units.rightText: And the priest shall offer the one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for her before Jehovah for the issue of her uncleanness.

units.leftText: You must keep the children of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die by defiling My tabernacle, which is among them.
units.rightText: Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is in the midst of them.

units.leftText: This is the law of him who has a discharge, of the man who has an emission of semen whereby he is unclean,
units.rightText: This is the law of him that hath an issue, and of him whose seed of copulation goeth from him, so that he is unclean thereby;

units.leftText: of a woman in her menstrual period, of any male or female who has a discharge, and of a man who lies with an unclean woman.’”
units.rightText: and of her that is sick with her impurity, and of him that hath an issue, of the man, and of the woman, and of him that lieth with her that is unclean.

units.leftText: Now the LORD spoke to Moses after the death of two of Aaron’s sons when they approached the presence of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they drew near before Jehovah, and died;

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Moses: “Tell your brother Aaron not to enter freely into the Most Holy Place behind the veil in front of the mercy seat on the ark, or else he will die, because I appear in the cloud above the mercy seat.
units.rightText: and Jehovah said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the veil, before the mercy-seat which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy-seat.
leftNotes: 16:2 Or the Holy Place; also in verses 16, 17, 20, 23, and 27
16:2 Or atonement cover; here and throughout this chapter

units.leftText: This is how Aaron is to enter the Holy Place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
units.rightText: Herewith shall Aaron come into the holy place: with a young bullock for a sin-offering, and a ram for a burnt-offering.

units.leftText: He is to wear the sacred linen tunic, with linen undergarments. He must tie a linen sash around him and put on the linen turban. These are holy garments, and he must bathe himself with water before he wears them.
units.rightText: He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded with the linen girdle, and with the linen mitre shall he be attired: they are the holy garments; and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and put them on.

units.leftText: And he shall take from the congregation of Israel two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
units.rightText: And he shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel two he-goats for a sin-offering, and one ram for a burnt-offering.

units.leftText: Aaron is to present the bull for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
units.rightText: And Aaron shall present the bullock of the sin-offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself, and for his house.

units.leftText: Then he shall take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: And he shall take the two goats, and set them before Jehovah at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: After Aaron casts lots for the two goats, one for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat,
units.rightText: And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for Jehovah, and the other lot for Azazel.
leftNotes: 16:8 Literally the other to Azazel; similarly twice in verse 10 and once in verse 26

units.leftText: he shall present the goat chosen by lot for the LORD and sacrifice it as a sin offering.
units.rightText: And Aaron shall present the goat upon which the lot fell for Jehovah, and offer him for a sin-offering.

units.leftText: But the goat chosen by lot as the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the LORD to make atonement by sending it into the wilderness as the scapegoat.
units.rightText: But the goat, on which the lot fell for Azazel, shall be set alive before Jehovah, to make atonement for him, to send him away for Azazel into the wilderness.

units.leftText: When Aaron presents the bull for his sin offering and makes atonement for himself and his household, he is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
units.rightText: And Aaron shall present the bullock of the sin-offering, which is for himself, and shall make atonement for himself, and for his house, and shall kill the bullock of the sin-offering which is for himself.

units.leftText: Then he must take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and take them inside the veil.
units.rightText: And he shall take a censer full of coals of fire from off the altar before Jehovah, and his hands full of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the veil:

units.leftText: He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of incense will cover the mercy seat above the Testimony, so that he will not die.
units.rightText: and he shall put the incense upon the fire before Jehovah, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy-seat that is upon the testimony, that he die not:
leftNotes: 16:13 The Testimony refers to the stone tablets in the ark of the covenant inscribed with the Ten Commandments.

units.leftText: And he is to take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat; then he shall sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the mercy seat.
units.rightText: and he shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the mercy-seat on the east; and before the mercy-seat shall he sprinkle of the blood with his finger seven times.

units.leftText: Aaron shall then slaughter the goat for the sin offering for the people and bring its blood behind the veil, and with its blood he must do as he did with the bull’s blood: He is to sprinkle it against the mercy seat and in front of it.
units.rightText: Then shall he kill the goat of the sin-offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the veil, and do with his blood as he did with the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy-seat, and before the mercy-seat:

units.leftText: So he shall make atonement for the Most Holy Place because of the impurities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins. He is to do the same for the Tent of Meeting which abides among them in the midst of their impurities.
units.rightText: and he shall make atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleannesses of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions, even all their sins: and so shall he do for the tent of meeting, that dwelleth with them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

units.leftText: No one may be in the Tent of Meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he leaves, after he has made atonement for himself, his household, and the whole assembly of Israel.
units.rightText: And there shall be no man in the tent of meeting when he goeth in to make atonement in the holy place, until he come out, and have made atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the assembly of Israel.

units.leftText: Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
units.rightText: And he shall go out unto the altar that is before Jehovah, and make atonement for it, and shall take of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about.

units.leftText: He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times to cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
units.rightText: And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallow it from the uncleannesses of the children of Israel.

units.leftText: When Aaron has finished purifying the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he is to bring forward the live goat.
units.rightText: And when he hath made an end of atoning for the holy place, and the tent of meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat:

units.leftText: Then he is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins. He is to put them on the goat’s head and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task.
units.rightText: and Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions, even all their sins; and he shall put them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of a man that is in readiness into the wilderness:

units.leftText: The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities into a solitary place, and the man will release it into the wilderness.
units.rightText: and the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a solitary land: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Then Aaron is to enter the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen garments he put on before entering the Most Holy Place, and leave them there.
units.rightText: And Aaron shall come into the tent of meeting, and shall put off the linen garments, which he put on when he went into the holy place, and shall leave them there:

units.leftText: He is to bathe himself with water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he must go out and sacrifice his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering to make atonement for himself and for the people.
units.rightText: and he shall bathe his flesh in water in a holy place, and put on his garments, and come forth, and offer his burnt-offering and the burnt-offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.

units.leftText: He is also to burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
units.rightText: And the fat of the sin-offering shall he burn upon the altar.

units.leftText: The man who released the goat as the scapegoat must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may reenter the camp.
units.rightText: And he that letteth go the goat for Azazel shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp.

units.leftText: The bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp; and their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned up.
units.rightText: And the bullock of the sin-offering, and the goat of the sin-offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall be carried forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.

units.leftText: The one who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and afterward he may reenter the camp.
units.rightText: And he that burneth them shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp.

units.leftText: This is to be a permanent statute for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall humble yourselves and not do any work — whether the native or the foreigner who resides among you —
units.rightText: And it shall be a statute for ever unto you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and shall do no manner of work, the home-born, or the stranger that sojourneth among you:
leftNotes: 16:29 Or afflict your souls or deny yourselves; also in verse 31

units.leftText: because on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, and you will be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
units.rightText: for on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins shall ye be clean before Jehovah.

units.leftText: It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, that you may humble yourselves; it is a permanent statute.
