units.rightText: Wherefore ye shall do my statutes, and keep mine ordinances and do them; and ye shall dwell in the land in safety.

units.leftText: Then the land will yield its fruit, so that you can eat your fill and dwell in safety in the land.
units.rightText: And the land shall yield its fruit, and ye shall eat your fill, and dwell therein in safety.

units.leftText: Now you may wonder, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?’
units.rightText: And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase;

units.leftText: But I will send My blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that the land will yield a crop sufficient for three years.
units.rightText: then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for the three years.

units.leftText: While you are sowing in the eighth year, you will be eating from the previous harvest, until the ninth year’s harvest comes in. The Law of Redemption
units.rightText: And ye shall sow the eighth year, and eat of the fruits, the old store; until the ninth year, until its fruits come in, ye shall eat the old store.

units.leftText: The land must not be sold permanently, because it is Mine, and you are but foreigners and residents with Me.
units.rightText: And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity; for the land is mine: for ye are strangers and sojourners with me.

units.leftText: Thus for every piece of property you possess, you must provide for the redemption of the land.
units.rightText: And in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land.

units.leftText: If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his property, his nearest of kin may come and redeem what his brother has sold.
units.rightText: If thy brother be waxed poor, and sell some of his possession, then shall his kinsman that is next unto him come, and shall redeem that which his brother hath sold.

units.leftText: Or if a man has no one to redeem it for him, but he prospers and acquires enough to redeem his land,
units.rightText: And if a man have no one to redeem it, and he be waxed rich and find sufficient to redeem it;

units.leftText: he shall calculate the years since its sale, repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.
units.rightText: then let him reckon the years of the sale thereof, and restore the overplus unto the man to whom he sold it; and he shall return unto his possession.

units.leftText: But if he cannot obtain enough to repay him, what he sold will remain in possession of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee, however, it is to be released, so that he may return to his property.
units.rightText: But if he be not able to get it back for himself, then that which he hath sold shall remain in the hand of him that hath bought it until the year of jubilee: and in the jubilee it shall go out, and he shall return unto his possession.

units.leftText: If a man sells a house in a walled city, he retains his right of redemption until a full year after its sale; during that year it may be redeemed.
units.rightText: And if a man sell a dwelling-house in a walled city, then he may redeem it within a whole year after it is sold; for a full year shall he have the right of redemption.

units.leftText: If it is not redeemed by the end of a full year, then the house in the walled city is permanently transferred to its buyer and his descendants. It is not to be released in the Jubilee.
units.rightText: And if it be not redeemed within the space of a full year, then the house that is in the walled city shall be made sure in perpetuity to him that bought it, throughout his generations: it shall not go out in the jubilee.

units.leftText: But houses in villages with no walls around them are to be considered as open fields. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
units.rightText: But the houses of the villages which have no wall round about them shall be reckoned with the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the jubilee.

units.leftText: As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites always have the right to redeem their houses in the cities they possess.
units.rightText: Nevertheless the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time.

units.leftText: So whatever belongs to the Levites may be redeemed— a house sold in a city they possess— and must be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
units.rightText: And if one of the Levites redeem, then the house that was sold, and the city of his possession, shall go out in the jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.

units.leftText: But the open pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for this is their permanent possession. Redemption of the Poor
units.rightText: But the field of the suburbs of their cities may not be sold; for it is their perpetual possession.

units.leftText: Now if your countryman becomes destitute and cannot support himself among you, then you are to help him as you would a foreigner or stranger, so that he can continue to live among you.
units.rightText: And if thy brother be waxed poor, and his hand fail with thee; then thou shalt uphold him: as a stranger and a sojourner shall he live with thee.

units.leftText: Do not take any interest or profit from him, but fear your God, that your countryman may live among you.
units.rightText: Take thou no interest of him or increase, but fear thy God; that thy brother may live with thee.

units.leftText: You must not lend him your silver at interest or sell him your food for profit.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not give him thy money upon interest, nor give him thy victuals for increase.

units.leftText: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God. Redemption of Bondmen
units.rightText: I am Jehovah your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.

units.leftText: If a countryman among you becomes destitute and sells himself to you, then you must not force him into slave labor.
units.rightText: And if thy brother be waxed poor with thee, and sell himself unto thee; thou shalt not make him to serve as a bondservant.

units.leftText: Let him stay with you as a hired worker or temporary resident; he is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
units.rightText: As a hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee; he shall serve with thee unto the year of jubilee:

units.leftText: Then he and his children are to be released, and he may return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.
units.rightText: then shall he go out from thee, he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.

units.leftText: Because the Israelites are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, they are not to be sold as slaves.
units.rightText: For they are my servants, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.

units.leftText: You are not to rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.
units.rightText: Thou shalt not rule over him with rigor, but shalt fear thy God.

units.leftText: Your menservants and maidservants shall come from the nations around you, from whom you may purchase them.
units.rightText: And as for thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, whom thou shalt have; of the nations that are round about you, of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.

units.leftText: You may also purchase them from the foreigners residing among you or their clans living among you who are born in your land. These may become your property.
units.rightText: Moreover of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they have begotten in your land: and they shall be your possession.

units.leftText: You may leave them to your sons after you to inherit as property; you can make them slaves for life. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, no man may rule harshly over his brother. Redemption of Servants
units.rightText: And ye shall make them an inheritance for your children after you, to hold for a possession; of them shall ye take your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule, one over another, with rigor.

units.leftText: If a foreigner residing among you prospers, but your countryman dwelling near him becomes destitute and sells himself to the foreigner or to a member of his clan,
units.rightText: And if a stranger or sojourner with thee be waxed rich, and thy brother be waxed poor beside him, and sell himself unto the stranger or sojourner with thee, or to the stock of the stranger’s family;

units.leftText: he retains the right of redemption after he has sold himself. One of his brothers may redeem him:
units.rightText: after that he is sold he may be redeemed: one of his brethren may redeem him;

units.leftText: either his uncle or cousin or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
units.rightText: or his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family may redeem him; or if he be waxed rich, he may redeem himself.

units.leftText: He and his purchaser will then count the time from the year he sold himself up to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale will be determined by the number of years, based on the daily wages of a hired hand.
units.rightText: And he shall reckon with him that bought him from the year that he sold himself to him unto the year of jubilee: and the price of his sale shall be according unto the number of years; according to the time of a hired servant shall he be with him.

units.leftText: If many years remain, he must pay for his redemption in proportion to his purchase price.
units.rightText: If there be yet many years, according unto them he shall give back the price of his redemption out of the money that he was bought for.

units.leftText: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he is to calculate and pay his redemption according to his remaining years.
units.rightText: And if there remain but few years unto the year of jubilee, then he shall reckon with him; according unto his years shall he give back the price of his redemption.

units.leftText: He shall be treated like a man hired from year to year, but a foreign owner must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
units.rightText: As a servant hired year by year shall he be with him: he shall not rule with rigor over him in thy sight.

units.leftText: Even if he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children shall be released in the Year of Jubilee.
units.rightText: And if he be not redeemed by these means, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee, he, and his children with him.

units.leftText: For the Israelites are My servants. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.[’’]
units.rightText: For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: “You must not make idols for yourselves or set up a carved image or sacred pillar; you must not place a sculpted stone in your land to bow down to it. For I am the LORD your God.
units.rightText: Ye shall make you no idols, neither shall ye rear you up a graven image, or a pillar, neither shall ye place any figured stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am Jehovah your God.

units.leftText: You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
units.rightText: Ye shall keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary: I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: If you follow My statutes and carefully keep My commandments,
units.rightText: If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them;

units.leftText: I will give you rains in their season, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.
units.rightText: then I will give your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.

units.leftText: Your threshing will continue until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will continue until sowing time; you will have your fill of food to eat and will dwell securely in your land.
units.rightText: And your threshing shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time; and ye shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land safely.

units.leftText: And I will give peace to the land, and you will lie down with nothing to fear. I will rid the land of dangerous animals, and no sword will pass through your land.
units.rightText: And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid: and I will cause evil beasts to cease out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.

units.leftText: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall by the sword before you.
units.rightText: And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.

units.leftText: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall by the sword before you.
units.rightText: And five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.

units.leftText: I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you.
units.rightText: And I will have respect unto you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and will establish my covenant with you.

units.leftText: You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.
units.rightText: And ye shall eat old store long kept, and ye shall bring forth the old because of the new.

units.leftText: And I will make My dwelling place among you, and My soul will not despise you.
units.rightText: And I will set my tabernacle among you: and my soul shall not abhor you.
leftNotes: 26:11 Or My tabernacle
26:11 Or reject; also in verse 30

units.leftText: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.
units.rightText: And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and ye shall be my people.
leftNotes: 26:12 Cited in 2 Corinthians 6:16|2CO 6:16*

units.leftText: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians. I broke the bars of your yoke and enabled you to walk in uprightness. Punishments for Disobedience (Leviticus 20:1–9|LEV 20:1-9*; Deuteronomy 28:15–68|DEU 28:15-68*)
units.rightText: I am Jehovah your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, that ye should not be their bondmen; and I have broken the bars of your yoke, and made you go upright.

units.leftText: If, however, you fail to obey Me and to carry out all these commandments,
units.rightText: But if ye will not hearken unto me, and will not do all these commandments;

units.leftText: and if you reject My statutes, despise My ordinances, and neglect to carry out all My commandments, and so break My covenant,
units.rightText: and if ye shall reject my statutes, and if your soul abhor mine ordinances, so that ye will not do all my commandments, but break my covenant;

units.leftText: then this is what I will do to you: I will bring upon you sudden terror, wasting disease, and fever that will destroy your sight and drain your life. You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.
units.rightText: I also will do this unto you: I will appoint terror over you, even consumption and fever, that shall consume the eyes, and make the soul to pine away; and ye shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.

units.leftText: And I will set My face against you, so that you will be defeated by your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one pursues you.
units.rightText: And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be smitten before your enemies: they that hate you shall rule over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.

units.leftText: And if after all this you will not obey Me, I will proceed to punish you sevenfold for your sins.
units.rightText: And if ye will not yet for these things hearken unto me, then I will chastise you seven times more for your sins.

units.leftText: I will break down your stubborn pride and make your sky like iron and your land like bronze,
units.rightText: And I will break the pride of your power: and I will make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass;

units.leftText: and your strength will be spent in vain. For your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.
units.rightText: and your strength shall be spent in vain; for your land shall not yield its increase, neither shall the trees of the land yield their fruit.

units.leftText: If you walk in hostility toward Me and refuse to obey Me, I will multiply your plagues seven times, according to your sins.
units.rightText: And if ye walk contrary unto me, and will not hearken unto me, I will bring seven times more plagues upon you according to your sins.

units.leftText: I will send wild animals against you to rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers, until your roads lie desolate.
units.rightText: And I will send the beast of the field among you, which shall rob you of your children, and destroy your cattle, and make you few in number; and your ways shall become desolate.

units.leftText: And if in spite of these things you do not accept My discipline, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,
units.rightText: And if by these things ye will not be reformed unto me, but will walk contrary unto me;

units.leftText: then I will act with hostility toward you, and I will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
units.rightText: then will I also walk contrary unto you; and I will smite you, even I, seven times for your sins.

units.leftText: And I will bring a sword against you to execute the vengeance of the covenant. Though you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
units.rightText: And I will bring a sword upon you, that shall execute the vengeance of the covenant; and ye shall be gathered together within your cities: and I will send the pestilence among you; and ye shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy.

units.leftText: When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole out your bread by weight, so that you will eat but not be satisfied.
units.rightText: When I break your staff of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall deliver your bread again by weight: and ye shall eat, and not be satisfied.
leftNotes: 26:26 Hebrew staff

units.leftText: But if in spite of all this you do not obey Me, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,
units.rightText: And if ye will not for all this hearken unto me, but walk contrary unto me;

units.leftText: then I will walk in fury against you, and I, even I, will punish you sevenfold for your sins.
units.rightText: then I will walk contrary unto you in wrath; and I also will chastise you seven times for your sins.

units.leftText: You will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And ye shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters shall ye eat.

units.leftText: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and heap your lifeless bodies on the lifeless remains of your idols; and My soul will despise you.
units.rightText: And I will destroy your high places, and cut down your sun-images, and cast your dead bodies upon the bodies of your idols; and my soul shall abhor you.

units.leftText: I will reduce your cities to rubble and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.
units.rightText: And I will make your cities a waste, and will bring your sanctuaries unto desolation, and I will not smell the savor of your sweet odors.

units.leftText: And I will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled.
units.rightText: And I will bring the land into desolation; and your enemies that dwell therein shall be astonished at it.

units.leftText: But I will scatter you among the nations and will draw out a sword after you as your land becomes desolate and your cities are laid waste.
units.rightText: And you will I scatter among the nations, and I will draw out the sword after you: and your land shall be a desolation, and your cities shall be a waste.

units.leftText: Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate, while you are in the land of your enemies. At that time the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
units.rightText: Then shall the land enjoy its sabbaths, as long as it lieth desolate, and ye are in your enemies’ land; even then shall the land rest, and enjoy its sabbaths.

units.leftText: As long as it lies desolate, the land will have the rest it did not receive during the Sabbaths when you lived in it.
units.rightText: As long as it lieth desolate it shall have rest, even the rest which it had not in your sabbaths, when ye dwelt upon it.

units.leftText: As for those of you who survive, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that even the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. And they will flee as one flees the sword, and fall when no one pursues them.
units.rightText: And as for them that are left of you, I will send a faintness into their heart in the lands of their enemies: and the sound of a driven leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as one fleeth from the sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.

units.leftText: They will stumble over one another as before the sword, though no one is behind them. So you will not be able to stand against your enemies.
units.rightText: And they shall stumble one upon another, as it were before the sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.

units.leftText: You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
units.rightText: And ye shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up.

units.leftText: Those of you who survive in the lands of your enemies will waste away in their iniquity and will decay in the sins of their fathers. God Remembers Those Who Repent
units.rightText: And they that are left of you shall pine away in their iniquity in your enemies’ lands; and also in the iniquities of their fathers shall they pine away with them.

units.leftText: But if they will confess their iniquity and that of their fathers in the unfaithfulness that they practiced against Me, by which they have also walked in hostility toward Me—
units.rightText: And they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, in their trespass which they trespassed against me, and also that, because they walked contrary unto me,

units.leftText: and I acted with hostility toward them and brought them into the land of their enemies— and if their uncircumcised hearts will be humbled and they will make amends for their iniquity,
units.rightText: I also walked contrary unto them, and brought them into the land of their enemies: if then their uncircumcised heart be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity;

units.leftText: then I will remember My covenant with Jacob and My covenant with Isaac and My covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.
units.rightText: then will I remember my covenant with Jacob; and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.

units.leftText: For the land will be abandoned by them, and it will enjoy its Sabbaths by lying desolate without them. And they will pay the penalty for their iniquity, because they rejected My ordinances and abhorred My statutes.
units.rightText: The land also shall be left by them, and shall enjoy its sabbaths, while it lieth desolate without them: and they shall accept of the punishment of their iniquity; because, even because they rejected mine ordinances, and their soul abhorred my statutes.

units.leftText: Yet in spite of this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject or despise them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.
units.rightText: And yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break my covenant with them; for I am Jehovah their God;

units.leftText: But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their fathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am the LORD.”
units.rightText: but I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God: I am Jehovah.

units.leftText: These are the statutes, ordinances, and laws that the LORD established between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
units.rightText: These are the statutes and ordinances and laws, which Jehovah made between him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by Moses.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Moses,
units.rightText: And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the value of persons,
units.rightText: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When a man shall accomplish a vow, the persons shall be for Jehovah by thy estimation.

units.leftText: if the valuation concerns a male from twenty to sixty years of age, then your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
units.rightText: And thy estimation shall be of the male from twenty years old even unto sixty years old, even thy estimation shall be fifty shekels of silver, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
leftNotes: 27:3 50 shekels is approximately 1.26 pounds or 569.8 grams of silver; also in verse 16.
27:3 A shekel weighed approximately 0.4 ounces or 11.4 grams; also in verse 25.

units.leftText: Or if it is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
units.rightText: And if it be a female, then thy estimation shall be thirty shekels.
leftNotes: 27:4 30 shekels is approximately 12 ounces or 342 grams of silver.

units.leftText: And if the person is from five to twenty years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
units.rightText: And if it be from five years old even unto twenty years old, then thy estimation shall be of the male twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
leftNotes: 27:5 20 shekels is approximately 8 ounces or 228 grams of silver.
27:5 10 shekels is approximately 4 ounces or 114 grams of silver; also in verse 7.

units.leftText: Now if the person is from one month to five years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female three shekels of silver.
units.rightText: And if it be from a month old even unto five years old, then thy estimation shall be of the male five shekels of silver, and for the female thy estimation shall be three shekels of silver.
leftNotes: 27:6 5 shekels is approximately 2 ounces or 57 grams of silver.
27:6 3 shekels is approximately 1.2 ounces or 34.2 grams of silver.

units.leftText: And if the person is sixty years of age or older, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels for the male and ten shekels for the female.
units.rightText: And if it be from sixty years old and upward; if it be a male, then thy estimation shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
leftNotes: 27:7 15 shekels is approximately 6 ounces or 171 grams of silver.

units.leftText: But if the one making the vow is too poor to pay the valuation, he is to present the person before the priest, who shall set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.
units.rightText: But if he be poorer than thy estimation, then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to the ability of him that vowed shall the priest value him.
leftNotes: 27:8 Or present himself

units.leftText: If he vows an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD shall be holy.
units.rightText: And if it be a beast, whereof men offer an oblation unto Jehovah, all that any man giveth of such unto Jehovah shall be holy.

units.leftText: He must not replace it or exchange it, either good for bad or bad for good. But if he does substitute one animal for another, both that animal and its substitute will be holy.
units.rightText: He shall not alter it, nor change it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good: and if he shall at all change beast for beast, then both it and that for which it is changed shall be holy.

units.leftText: But if the vow involves any of the unclean animals that may not be brought as an offering to the LORD, the animal must be presented before the priest.
units.rightText: And if it be any unclean beast, of which they do not offer an oblation unto Jehovah, then he shall set the beast before the priest;

units.leftText: The priest shall set its value, whether high or low; as the priest values it, the price will be set.
units.rightText: and the priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad: as thou the priest valuest it, so shall it be.

units.leftText: If, however, the owner decides to redeem the animal, he must add a fifth to its value.
units.rightText: But if he will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part thereof unto thy estimation.

units.leftText: Now if a man consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, then the priest shall value it either as good or bad. The price will stand just as the priest values it.
units.rightText: And when a man shall sanctify his house to be holy unto Jehovah, then the priest shall estimate it, whether it be good or bad: as the priest shall estimate it, so shall it stand.

units.leftText: But if he who consecrated his house redeems it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it will belong to him.
units.rightText: And if he that sanctified it will redeem his house, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of thy estimation unto it, and it shall be his.

units.leftText: If a man consecrates to the LORD a parcel of his land, then your valuation shall be proportional to the seed required for it — fifty shekels of silver for every homer of barley seed.
units.rightText: And if a man shall sanctify unto Jehovah part of the field of his possession, then thy estimation shall be according to the sowing thereof: the sowing of a homer of barley shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver.
leftNotes: 27:16 A homer is a dry measure of approximately 6.24 bushels or 220 liters (probably about 291 pounds or 132 kilograms of barley seed).

units.leftText: If he consecrates his field during the Year of Jubilee, the price will stand according to your valuation.
units.rightText: If he sanctify his field from the year of jubilee, according to thy estimation it shall stand.

units.leftText: But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, the priest is to calculate the price in proportion to the years left until the next Year of Jubilee, so that your valuation will be reduced.
units.rightText: But if he sanctify his field after the jubilee, then the priest shall reckon unto him the money according to the years that remain unto the year of jubilee; and an abatement shall be made from thy estimation.

units.leftText: And if the one who consecrated the field decides to redeem it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it shall belong to him.
units.rightText: And if he that sanctified the field will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of thy estimation unto it, and it shall be assured to him.

units.leftText: If, however, he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to another man, it may no longer be redeemed.
units.rightText: And if he will not redeem the field, or if he have sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed any more:

units.leftText: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD; it becomes the property of the priests.
units.rightText: but the field, when it goeth out in the jubilee, shall be holy unto Jehovah, as a field devoted; the possession thereof shall be the priest’s.

units.leftText: Now if a man consecrates to the LORD a field he has purchased, which is not a part of his own property,
units.rightText: And if he sanctify unto Jehovah a field which he hath bought, which is not of the field of his possession;

units.leftText: then the priest shall calculate for him the value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man shall pay the assessed value on that day as a sacred offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: then the priest shall reckon unto him the worth of thy estimation unto the year of jubilee: and he shall give thine estimation in that day, as a holy thing unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought — the original owner of the land.
units.rightText: In the year of jubilee the field shall return unto him of whom it was bought, even to him to whom the possession of the land belongeth.

units.leftText: Every valuation will be according to the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.
units.rightText: And all thy estimations shall be according to the shekel of the sanctuary: twenty gerahs shall be the shekel.
leftNotes: 27:25 20 gerahs is equivalent to one shekel (approximately 0.4 ounces or 11.4 grams).

units.leftText: But no one may consecrate a firstborn of the livestock, because a firstborn belongs to the LORD. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it is the LORD’s.
units.rightText: Only the firstling among beasts, which is made a firstling to Jehovah, no man shall sanctify it; whether it be ox or sheep, it is Jehovah’s.

units.leftText: But if it is among the unclean animals, then he may redeem it according to your valuation and add a fifth of its value. If it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.
units.rightText: And if it be of an unclean beast, then he shall ransom it according to thine estimation, and shall add unto it the fifth part thereof: or if it be not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to thy estimation.

units.leftText: Nothing that a man sets apart to the LORD from all he owns — whether a man, an animal, or his inherited land — can be sold or redeemed; everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.
units.rightText: Notwithstanding, no devoted thing, that a man shall devote unto Jehovah of all that he hath, whether of man or beast, or of the field of his possession, shall be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy unto Jehovah.
leftNotes: 27:28 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD; similarly in verse 29.

units.leftText: No person set apart for destruction may be ransomed; he must surely be put to death. Instruction on Tithes (Deuteronomy 14:22–29|DEU 14:22-29*; Deuteronomy 26:1–15|DEU 26:1-15*; Nehemiah 13:10–14|NEH 13:10-14*)
units.rightText: No one devoted, that shall be devoted from among men, shall be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: Thus any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
units.rightText: And all the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree, is Jehovah’s: it is holy unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: If a man wishes to redeem part of his tithe, he must add a fifth to its value.
units.rightText: And if a man will redeem aught of his tithe, he shall add unto it the fifth part thereof.

units.leftText: Every tenth animal from the herd or flock that passes under the shepherd’s rod will be holy to the LORD.
units.rightText: And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatsoever passeth under the rod, the tenth shall be holy unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: He must not inspect whether it is good or bad, and he shall not make any substitution. But if he does make a substitution, both the animal and its substitute shall become holy; they cannot be redeemed.’”
units.rightText: He shall not search whether it be good or bad, neither shall he change it: and if he change it at all, then both it and that for which it is changed shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.

units.leftText: These are the commandments that the LORD gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
units.rightText: These are the commandments, which Jehovah commanded Moses for the children of Israel in mount Sinai.
